frozen_r2_hypothesis_decisions.interpretation: The mechanistic core is already well represented by prior art. The remaining potentially differentiating element is the controlled directional gap-size response within the exact polymer-separated Ag-bridge architecture. That narrower question is not substituted for the frozen hypothesis and is recorded only as a residual question; therefore the hypothesis is retained as a bounded literature-supported extension, not as a high-novelty core claim.
frozen_r2_hypothesis_decisions.residual_question: Under matched analyte access, excitation, loading, acquisition, and structural-integrity conditions, does controlled variation of the polymer-defined inner/outer Ag gap in the Ag-bridge architecture produce a reproducible directional SERS trend?
frozen_r2_hypothesis_decisions.title: Nanogap-mediated hotspot coupling in Au/Ag architectures

frozen_r2_hypothesis_decisions.interpretation: The mode-matching mechanism is not a new relation for this platform: the source paper itself invokes resonance matching as the LSPR shifts toward the fixed 532 nm excitation. However, that study does not vary excitation wavelength. Independent multiwavelength SERS studies show wavelength-dependent, substrate-specific behavior rather than a universal monotonic increase with excitation wavelength. The hypothesis is therefore rejected as formulated because its distinctive directional prediction is unsupported, not because mode matching is scientifically implausible.
frozen_r2_hypothesis_decisions.residual_question: A reformulated wavelength-response experiment could test a resonance profile across multiple excitation wavelengths, but creating that reformulation would be a new hypothesis and is outside frozen R2.
frozen_r2_hypothesis_decisions.title: Excitation-mode matching as a design-context interaction

frozen_r2_hypothesis_decisions.interpretation: Prior art directly shows that dispersed and drying-accumulated Ag-shell core-satellite measurement configurations can differ strongly in SERS intensity and reproducibility, so the broad context effect is not novel. The frozen paired-context relation remains unresolved because the available study does not measure the same analyte-mixed preparation before and after drying, and it does not establish a qualitative peak-profile transformation. This is the strongest remaining relational-gap candidate among the three, but it remains a testable hypothesis rather than an established effect.
frozen_r2_hypothesis_decisions.residual_question: For the same analyte-mixed Ag-shell core-satellite preparation, does a paired solution-to-dried transition reproducibly change normalized peak-intensity distribution or peak profile after controlling concentration, acquisition, and hotspot sampling?
frozen_r2_hypothesis_decisions.title: Measurement-context dependence of Au/Ag SERS response
